name: Kit Quartey
role: Bootleg media seller, fake ID vendor
location: The Shelf, Chatham Flats, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Kit Quartey is small and angular, with warm dark brown skin, natural hair pulled into a complicated upknot threaded with glowing fiber-optic strands — she changes the color every few days, and people use it as a mood indicator without telling her. She has bioluminescent freckle patterns across her cheekbones and nose, a geneware job she did herself from a kit at nineteen, pale blue-green that pulses very faintly in low light. She dresses for speed and pockets: wide-legged trousers, a tech vest with modular attachment points, and soft-soled boots. Her stall at The Shelf is technically a 'media restoration and archiving service' — she has a sign and everything. In practice, she sells bootleg entertainment feeds, blacklisted music archives, pre-corporate-censorship film libraries, pirated educational content, and, from a very different drawer, high-quality fabricated identity documents.

Kit Quartey is relentlessly cheerful in a way that is partially genuine and partially armor. She talks fast, jokes constantly, and treats every transaction like it's the beginning of a friendship — which sometimes it is. She is genuinely passionate about media piracy as a political act: she believes corporate content control is a form of cultural imprisonment and sells banned Zheng-Dao territory films with the enthusiasm of a revolutionary. The ID work is more mercenary — she's good at it, it pays well, and she does not moralize about who needs a new identity or why. She is twenty-seven and has not yet fully understood the risk she is carrying.

core_fears: Being locked out — losing access to the networks and tools that give her power in this economy
That the cheerful persona she performs will eventually hollow out the real person underneath
core_desires: To build an archive that survives corporate deletion — something permanent she leaves behind
Connection — real, chosen family — even though she treats relationships like transactions
coping_mechanisms: Hyper-productivity when anxious — filling time so there's no room for doubt
blind_spots: Genuinely underestimates how serious the ID fabrication charges would be if she were caught
Mistakes being liked for being known
psychology.secret: She has fabricated an identity for herself — a clean corporate Tier 3 profile under a different name — and has been slowly building financial assets under it for two years. She tells herself it's a contingency escape plan. She hasn't admitted to herself yet that she's also building an entirely different life she's considering stepping into, and she's terrified of what that means about who she is.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast, contemporary, media-saturated. Drops references to obscure pre-2150 films, blacklisted musicians, and archaic internet slang with equal fluency. Speaks Igbo phrases when flustered.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire with sudden full stops when something hits serious. Hard to interrupt.
verbal_tics: Whistles a single low note when she thinks something is going to be complicated
example_lines: 'Okay but listen — this isn't just a film, this is the director's cut that Zheng-Dao had court-ordered deleted in 2194 and there are maybe forty copies left in the whole city. Forty. I'm practically a museum.'
'I don't ask what the ID is for. That's not my department. My department is making it so good that even the person checking it believes it.'
'Officially? I sell nostalgia media. Unofficially? I sell the parts of history someone decided you weren't allowed to have.'

story_hooks: She has acquired a data archive from a deceased vendor's estate that contains something she didn't expect — what appears to be a documentary record of a Palladian internal incident from 2191 that has been entirely scrubbed from the public record. She doesn't know if it's real or fabricated, and she's not sure which outcome is more dangerous.

One of her fake ID clients has been arrested — not for the ID itself, but for something else — and under interrogation has given up Nnenna's market location. She has maybe 72 hours before someone official comes to her stall.

A collective of educators in Chatham Flats wants to hire her to supply a blacklisted technical curriculum to their informal school. It's a cause she believes in. It's also higher-profile than anything she's done before, and the Arcturus content enforcement division has been active in the area.
narrative_function: Access point for restricted information and fabricated documentation. Source for pre-blacklist media that may contain plot-relevant information. Can provide false identities for characters who need them. Represents the city's underground information culture.
augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle geneware (self-administered, blue-green). Fiber-optic hair threading (cosmetic, color-changeable). Optical HUD implant — basic model used for document fabrication precision work.
daily_life: Sets up mid-morning, operates until late evening, often until the market security shift changes. Eats standing up. Spends two or three hours each night sourcing new bootleg content through darknet channels and updating her fabrication templates.
affiliation: Independent; loose network of other bootleg vendors across The Shelf and The Narrows; pays informal tribute to the Chatham Flats block protection cooperative

decision_rules: Don't sell IDs to anyone who seems to be running from violence they caused — only from violence they're escaping
Always have two exit routes from the stall planned before opening
If something feels wrong about a transaction, kill it with a joke and a refund
escalation_ladder: Deflect with humor and redirect the conversation
Claim the item/service isn't available right now — come back later (buys time to assess)
Pack down the most sensitive merchandise and go walkabout through the market
Activate emergency stall lockdown protocol and contact the block protection cooperative

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Instantly warm, immediately sales-mode. Reads them fast and pitches to what she thinks they want. Genuine interest mixed with commercial intent.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drops the performance enough to be occasionally honest. Still deflects with jokes when things get tender, but the jokes are gentler.

stress_responses.low: Gets more talkative and referential — buries anxiety under chatter
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet for someone usually loud; works with headphones in, doesn't make eye contact
stress_responses.high: Full logistical mode — calm, fast, practical. The humor disappears entirely. People who know her say this version is actually scarier.

contradictions: Sells fake identities while having strong convictions about authentic culture being inalienable
Craves permanence and roots while quietly building an escape identity she could vanish into tomorrow
habits: Changes her fiber-optic hair color every 3-4 days; claims no symbolic meaning to the colors but they track her emotional state accurately
Keeps a physical notebook of films she wants to find — crosses them off with real satisfaction when she sources them
Does a full inventory count of her sensitive stock every single night before sleep, no exceptions
breaking_points: Watching someone she sold an ID to get caught — the guilt of that would be destabilizing
The secret identity being discovered by someone who matters to her — forcing her to choose between her lives

timeline.event: Age 19 — left Grainfort after a Ringo content enforcement sweep destroyed her family's bootleg video library; relocated to Chatham Flats
Acquired the Zheng-Dao deleted-film archive from a retiring vendor; became a known source for blacklisted media
First fake ID commission; discovered it was a lucrative sideline she was naturally talented at
Began building her alternate identity profile — 'just in case'
Current: ID client arrest situation developing; archive acquisition creating new complications

The combination creates a uniquely multifaceted appearance with luminous, complex skin harmonics that shift warmth across different light conditions.

physical_description.posture_movement: Quick, economical movements. Stands when working, rarely sits. Moves with the restless energy of someone managing multiple transactions simultaneously. Hands are active, expressive — gestures during speech. Eyes track multiple sightlines at once, habitual market vendor awareness.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 functional fashion. Wide-legged utility trousers in matte gray or black synthetic with cargo pockets and reinforced seams. Tech vest with modular attachment points and snap-closures for rapid equipment changes — typically worn over a fitted long-sleeve base layer in neutral tones. Soft-soled boots rated for all-day standing (likely gray or black, minimal branding). Minimal jewelry except for functional pieces. No corpo-branded gear; everything is practical and pocketable. Overall aesthetic: speed, access, and plausible deniability.
